exercises.name: Rolling Like a Ball
instructions: Sit near the front of the mat, hug your shins, and open your knees to shoulder width.
Round your spine, tuck your chin toward your chest, and lift your feet to balance behind your sitting bones.
Breathe in and roll back as far as your shoulder blades, keeping the same round shape.
Breathe out and roll up to the balance without letting your feet touch the floor.
exercises.formCue: Stay a ball: heels close, chin tucked.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rolling onto the neck or head, and throwing the legs or head to get back up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold behind the thighs with a looser shape, or just practise the balance without rolling.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the abdominals to hold a rounded spine and control momentum.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back, hug both knees in, and curl your head and shoulders off the mat.
Keep one knee in and reach the other leg out to about 45 degrees.
Place the outside hand on the ankle and the inside hand on the knee of the bent leg.
Switch legs smoothly, drawing each knee in as the other leg reaches long.
Keep your lower back on the mat and your trunk still for the whole set.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rocking the torso side to side, or letting the head drop and the neck take the strain.
exercises.beginnerModification: Reach the straight leg higher toward the ceiling, or rest your head on the mat.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches the trunk to stay stable while the legs move.

exercises.name: Double-Leg Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back, hug both knees to your chest, and curl your head and shoulders up.
Breathe in and reach your arms back by your ears and both legs out on a high diagonal.
Keep your lower back on the mat and your head and shoulders lifted.
Breathe out, circle your arms around, and hug your knees back in.
Repeat without lowering your head between reps.
exercises.formCue: Reach long, hug tight, back stays down.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the lower back arch as the legs reach, or dropping the head back with the arms.
exercises.beginnerModification: Reach the legs straight up instead of out, or move only the arms and then only the legs.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the abdominal strength to hold the trunk steady against long levers.

exercises.name: Single Straight-Leg Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back, curl your head and shoulders up, and reach both legs toward the ceiling.
Hold behind the calf or thigh of one leg and lower the other leg toward the mat.
Draw the top leg toward you with two small pulses.
Switch legs in a scissor action, keeping both knees as straight as you can.
Keep your elbows wide and your trunk still throughout.
exercises.formCue: Legs scissor, trunk does not rock.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bouncing the torso with each pulse, or rounding the shoulders forward to reach the leg.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold behind the thigh, soften the knees, and keep the lower leg higher off the mat.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the abdominals while giving the hamstrings an active stretch.

exercises.name: Double Straight-Leg Stretch
exercises.musclesWorked: Lower abdominals, hip flexors, inner thighs
instructions: Lie on your back with hands layered behind your head, elbows wide, and head and shoulders curled up.
Reach both legs straight up and squeeze them together.
Lower both legs only as far as your lower back stays on the mat.
Lift the legs back to vertical with a little more emphasis on the way up.
Keep your chest lifted and neck relaxed for every rep.
exercises.formCue: Lower slow, lift with intent, back stays down.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the lower back arch off the mat, or losing the shoulder lift as the legs lower.
exercises.beginnerModification: Bend the knees slightly, lower only a short way, and place your hands under your hips.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It loads the lower abdominals hard while the trunk learns to resist arching.

exercises.name: Criss-Cross
instructions: Lie on your back with hands behind your head, elbows wide, and knees bent over your hips.
Curl your head and shoulders up and reach one leg out on a diagonal.
Rotate your ribcage toward the bent knee, lifting the back of the opposite shoulder off the mat.
Hold the twist for a beat, then switch sides as you change legs.
Keep your hips still and your elbows open the whole time.
exercises.formCue: Twist the ribs, not the elbows.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pulling on the neck and flapping the elbows instead of rotating the trunk, or rocking the hips.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep both feet on the floor with knees bent and twist the upper body only.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds rotational strength in the obliques with the pelvis held steady.

exercises.name: Spine Stretch Forward
instructions: Sit tall with legs straight, a little wider than your hips, and feet flexed.
Reach your arms forward at shoulder height.
Breathe out, nod your chin, and round forward one segment at a time while pulling your stomach back.
Reach forward as if curving over a big ball, keeping your hips where they are.
Breathe in and stack your spine back up to tall sitting.
exercises.formCue: Round up and over, belly pulls back.
exercises.commonMistakes: Starting slumped, or hinging flat from the hips instead of rounding the spine.
exercises.beginnerModification: Sit on a folded blanket or bend your knees so you can start upright.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches the spine to move one segment at a time and stretches the back of the body.

exercises.name: Open-Leg Rocker
exercises.musclesWorked: Abdominals, hip flexors, hamstrings, spinal erectors
instructions: Sit just behind your sitting bones, hold your ankles, and straighten your legs into a V at shoulder width.
Keep your lower back gently rounded and your chest lifted.
Tilt your pelvis under to start rolling back and roll only as far as your shoulder blades.
Roll back up using your abdominals and pause in the balance.
Keep your arms straight and the shape the same in both directions.
exercises.formCue: The pelvis starts the roll, not the head.
exercises.commonMistakes: Throwing the head back to start, or rolling onto the neck.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold behind your calves or thighs with bent knees, or just hold the V balance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It combines balance, hamstring length, and abdominal control in one rolling movement.

exercises.name: Corkscrew
exercises.musclesWorked: Abdominals, obliques, hip flexors, inner thighs
instructions: Lie on your back with arms long by your sides, palms pressing down, and both legs straight up and squeezed together.
Keep your whole spine on the mat and your shoulders wide.
Circle both legs as one: over to one side, down and around, and up the other side.
Pause at the top, then reverse the circle.
Keep the circle small enough that your lower back and hips stay still.
exercises.formCue: Legs glued together, small circle, quiet hips.
exercises.commonMistakes: Making the circle so big that the lower back arches or the hips roll off the mat.
exercises.beginnerModification: Bend the knees a little, make a plate-sized circle, and put your hands under your hips.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the trunk to stay anchored while the legs move through rotation.

exercises.name: Saw
exercises.musclesWorked: Obliques, spinal erectors, hamstrings, upper back
instructions: Sit tall with legs straight and a little wider than the mat, feet flexed, and arms out to the sides.
Rotate your trunk to one side while both sitting bones stay down.
Reach the front hand toward the outside of the opposite foot as the back arm reaches behind you.
Round forward over the leg and breathe out fully.
Roll up, untwist to the centre, and repeat to the other side.
exercises.formCue: Both hips stay heavy as you twist and reach.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the opposite hip lift or slide forward, or collapsing the chest instead of rotating.
exercises.beginnerModification: Sit on a folded blanket and bend the knees slightly.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It pairs spinal rotation with a hamstring stretch and trains a full breath out.

exercises.name: Swan Prep
exercises.musclesWorked: Spinal erectors, glutes, upper back, triceps
instructions: Lie face down with hands under your shoulders, elbows close to your sides, and legs together.
Lift your stomach lightly off the mat and press your hip bones down.
Lift your head and chest using your upper back, with only light pressure in the hands.
Press into your hands to rise a little higher while your neck stays long.
Lower slowly, lengthening forward as you go.
exercises.formCue: Chest reaches forward and up, belly lifted.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pushing up with the arms and hinging in the lower back, or throwing the head back.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep your forearms on the mat and lift only a few centimetres.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds upper-back extension strength to balance all the forward-rounding work.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Kick
instructions: Lie face down and prop yourself on your forearms with elbows under your shoulders.
Press your elbows down, lift your chest, and pull your stomach up off the mat.
Kick one heel toward your seat with two quick pulses.
Straighten that leg to the mat and kick the other heel.
Keep your hips and trunk completely still as the legs alternate.
exercises.formCue: Chest proud, hips pinned, heel to seat.
exercises.commonMistakes: Sinking between the shoulders, or letting the hips rock with each kick.
exercises.beginnerModification: Rest your forehead on stacked hands and kick once per side.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the hamstrings and upper back while opening the front of the thighs.

exercises.name: Double-Leg Kick
exercises.musclesWorked: Spinal erectors, glutes, hamstrings, rear shoulders
instructions: Lie face down with one cheek on the mat and hands clasped high on your back, elbows relaxed down.
Kick both heels toward your seat three times.
Straighten your legs to the mat as you reach your clasped hands toward your heels and lift your chest.
Keep your stomach lifted and your neck long at the top.
Lower, turn your head to the other cheek, and repeat.
exercises.formCue: Reach the hands to the heels and let the chest follow.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the stomach sag so the lower back pinches, or craning the neck up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep the hands by your hips instead of clasped, and lift the chest only slightly.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It opens the chest and shoulders while strengthening the whole back line.

exercises.name: Teaser
exercises.musclesWorked: Abdominals, hip flexors, quads, spinal erectors
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs together on a 45 degree diagonal and arms reaching overhead.
Bring your arms forward, lift your head, and roll up one segment at a time.
Finish in a V with your fingers reaching toward your toes and your chest open.
Hold for a breath with your legs still.
Roll down slowly through the lower back first, keeping the legs where they are.
exercises.formCue: Legs stay still, the spine does the moving.
exercises.commonMistakes: Jerking up with momentum, letting the legs drop, or hinging with a stiff arched back.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use Teaser Prep with the knees bent and feet on the floor, or one leg extended.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is the benchmark of Pilates control: strength, balance, and spinal articulation together.

exercises.name: Leg Pull Back
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, rear shoulders, triceps, core
instructions: Sit with legs straight and hands on the mat behind your hips, fingers pointing forward or out.
Press down through your hands and heels and lift your hips until your body is one straight line.
Keep your hips level and kick one straight leg up toward the ceiling.
Lower it with control and switch legs.
Finish the set, then lower your hips slowly to the mat.
exercises.formCue: Hips stay high and level as the leg lifts.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the hips drop as the leg kicks, or sinking into the shoulders and wrists.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold the reverse plank without the kicks, or bend the knees into a tabletop.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the back of the body and opens the chest and shoulders.

exercises.name: Seal
instructions: Sit with knees bent and open and heels together.
Thread your hands between your legs and hold the outsides of your ankles.
Lift your feet and balance just behind your sitting bones with a rounded spine.
Roll back to your shoulder blades, then roll up and find the balance again.
Add three small foot claps at the back and at the front once the roll is smooth.
exercises.formCue: Round and roll, pause in the balance.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rolling onto the neck, or using a kick of the legs to get back up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Leave out the claps and hold behind the thighs.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It loosens the back at the end of a mat session and keeps the balance sharp.

exercises.name: Pilates Side Bend
exercises.musclesWorked: Obliques, shoulders, outer hips, inner thighs
instructions: Sit on one hip with knees bent, top foot just in front of the bottom foot, and your bottom hand on the mat under your shoulder.
Press into your hand and feet and lift your hips as you straighten your legs.
Reach your top arm overhead so your body makes a long arc.
Keep the supporting shoulder away from your ear and your chest open.
Lower your hips with control to just above the mat and repeat before switching sides.
exercises.formCue: Push the floor away and lift from the underside of the waist.
exercises.commonMistakes: Sinking into the wrist and shoulder, or letting the top shoulder roll forward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep the bottom knee on the mat, or work from the forearm.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds side-body and shoulder strength with control through a full range.

exercises.name: Neck Pull
exercises.musclesWorked: Abdominals, hip flexors, spinal erectors, hamstrings
instructions: Lie on your back with legs straight and hip-width apart, feet flexed, and hands layered behind your head.
Keep your elbows wide, curl your head and chest up, and roll forward over your legs.
Stack your spine up to sit tall, pressing your head lightly back into your hands.
Lean back in one straight line as far as you can control.
Round your lower back and roll down to the mat one segment at a time.
exercises.formCue: Elbows wide, legs heavy, no tugging on the head.
exercises.commonMistakes: Yanking on the neck to get up, or letting the feet lift off the mat.
exercises.beginnerModification: Bend the knees slightly, or do a Roll-Up with the arms reaching forward.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is a harder Roll-Up that demands full abdominal control with no help from the arms.
